reason: The two candidates are nearly identical. Both crop the photo down to the wrapped fists and lose the torso. Both also show a visible seam or band in the background below the X-row, around y≈380, which looks stitched rather than designed. In both, the 'W' of WIN sits about 12px from the left edge and the LUST/WIN letter-spacing stretches almost the full width, so the type feels cramped against the edges. The corner X marks sit at arbitrary heights instead of at the canvas corners. Neither candidate is clearly better: A's WIN tracking is a little wider and B's is a little tighter, which doesn't change the result.

I can't see a meaningful difference between A and B; they look the same apart from about a pixel of offset. Both have the same flaws. The crane photo is gone. The pink brush-stroke highlight sits loose above the headline instead of behind it, and a stray brush fragment is left under the brick image. The body copy is cramped right against the top of the brick image, the image fills a narrow column with wide empty side margins, and nothing anchors the layout as a newsletter sign-up.

A keeps the red panel, the type hierarchy and the photo intact, but it places the panel in the middle of the photo. That leaves a stray left strip of a man that reads as a separate image and crowds the dotted pattern. The text block is also small for the banner height. B loses almost all the imagery to a sliver with half-cut faces. Its shopping-bag icon is oversized and cut off from the headline, there's an odd dotted bar, and the rule line runs through the '2018' date. 'Tickets are available' is jammed beside the date on that line, which breaks the original's structure.

Both are nearly the same layout. The red panel is shrunk into the top-left 40% and the photo is cropped so badly that the red panel hides the attendees' faces. That leaves the bottom half as dead table clutter: hands, bottles and a pale translucent rectangle. The headline, date and 'Tickets are available' text are all small for the canvas, and the format is used poorly. A's panel is flush against the top edge and its dot grid runs off the canvas, which looks cramped. B pulls the panel and dots in with a small, consistent top margin, so it feels slightly more deliberate, though it shows an odd strip of photo above the panel.

The two are nearly identical. Both right-align the text stack (July 29, Sewing Class, For Beginners and the Grove.Online ribbon) but centre the illustration cluster under it, so the column has two different axes. The ribbon floats far below the art, the empty band at the bottom is large, and the text is small at this skyscraper size. A uses the height a little better: its illustration is larger and there are fewer empty bands. B's illustration is smaller and its 'For Beginners' line sits tighter under the headline, so it leaves more empty space at the bottom.

Both use the same weak layout. The headline is shrunk into a narrow right column with a big dead gap between 'CHILDREN'S' and 'DAY', which breaks the headline into separate pieces. The left half is mostly empty yellow with a stray pink block, and the green dot overlaps the train. A is worse because the first digit of the address ('12231') is clipped or hidden at the left edge. B shows the full address, but it is still tiny and the date block sits in a sparse area.

Both use the same broken layout. The address is crammed into a three-line column at a tiny size next to the date, so the address/date/URL block is jumbled. The second model photo floats loose below the pattern panel with large empty white margins on either side, and her head is cropped off. The left photo sticks out of the panel's left edge, and keaton.us is tiny. A sits a little more evenly in the canvas; B is pushed up, leaving more dead space at the bottom.

Both use the same broken layout. The photo is cropped to half a face, with one eye, and the blue panel covers most of the model. The thin outline frame floats loose over the foliage instead of framing the panel. '14' is split away from 'August', and 'FREE JOIN' wraps onto two lines. A spreads the panel content more evenly. B pushes 'August' up against the panel's top edge and leaves a large empty block of blue at the bottom.

Both break the original's even three-bar stack. The NEW YORK bar is much bigger than SUBWAY and GUIDE, its text is indented differently from the other two, and the grey stripe shapes float in the middle of the photo as a broken 'A' glyph, with a faint ghost copy at the left. A also spreads the bars apart with uneven gaps (larger before GUIDE). B keeps the bars in a tighter, more even group closer to the original, but still has the same size mismatch and the stray shapes.

Both break the original's three equal stacked ribbons. NEW YORK is a big band, while SUBWAY and GUIDE are small stubs with a different text indent, so the title no longer reads as one block. In both, the beige diagonal shapes are broken into arbitrary floating fragments, the photo is cropped so the sign reads 'BWAY', and the bottom third is dead space. A spaces the ribbons further apart, which scatters the title. B keeps them tight and near the top, closer to the original, but its fragments sit on the sign's 'B' with a stray ghost shape, so the two are almost equivalent.

Both use the same bad crop: the crucifix's head and left arm are cut off at the left edge, and the original full-canvas inset frame has turned into a stray thin rectangle floating mid-canvas across the cross. A's frame sits a little lower and its text sits low, with 'CHURCH SERVICE' near the bottom edge. B's text block sits slightly higher and is better balanced, but it still has the same broken frame and crop.

Both fail in the same ways. The photo is shrunk to a small thumbnail jammed against the right edge, and the pink corner triangle now cuts across the model's face. The left half of the canvas is dead black. The three pink bars are offset to the right with uneven gaps (a tight LomoArt–Fashion gap, then a bigger one before Photography), and their tiny text has no clear hierarchy. B is shifted lower, which spreads the empty space slightly more evenly from top to bottom than A's large empty bottom, but neither layout was actually rearranged.

A and B look pixel-identical, and they share the same flaws. The bunny-on-bike illustration is cropped at both side edges, cutting off the basket and the bike wheels. The 'FUN GROUP' text is oversized and wraps onto two lines, and it sits right on top of the busy bike illustration, which is a clear text-on-image collision. The headline is small compared with the original, and there is a dead gap between the headline and the bunny.

The two are almost identical. Both have the same flaws: the header row (logo, tagline, address) is shrunk to roughly 9px and is barely readable; the middle headline line 'a daring adventure or' nearly touches both side edges; and there is a lot of empty sky above the header. These make both look like a shrunk-and-cropped copy rather than a real tall-format rearrangement. The only difference is the 'Helen Keller' attribution: in A it sits a little too far below the quote and starts to drift away from it, while B keeps it closer to the quote, as in the original.

Both candidates are unusable, and they are almost identical. Each one loses the teal photo background and the entire quote ('Dogs never bite me — just humans.' / Marilyn Monroe), leaving an empty white frame with scattered faint icons. The teal block, the photo thumbnail and a pile of dog icons are dumped in a strip along the bottom edge. Neither keeps the message, the hierarchy or the brand feel.

A is a faithful, uniform scale-down with the original's layout. Its headline is tight to the side edges (about 10px margins), and the nurse illustration seems to stop just short of the bottom edge instead of running off it cleanly. B has the same tight headline, but it lifts the nurse higher, so the illustration ends in a hard horizontal line with a visible purple strip below it and looks cut off and floating. The chevrons also crowd the nurse's cap in B.

Both use the same broken layout. The doodle frame is left empty and 'WE LOVE YOU!' is pulled out of it and shrunk, so the headline is lost. The text is crammed into a tight stack with no spacing, and the reading order is jumbled: 'DEAR TEACHERS!' sits below the school name and the headline comes before the event title. A is slightly better because its block sits nearer the middle (about 97px above, 105px below), while B is pushed up and leaves a bigger empty area at the bottom.

Both candidates have nearly the same layout and the same flaws. The hero photo has become a small, washed-out strip floating in a big empty white column. The yellow highlight bars have moved away from the headline and sit as loose fragments at the bottom, and the circle motif has shrunk to specks. The headline sits off-centre in empty space, so the original's layered photo-and-text composition is lost. The only differences are tiny: the semicircle and headline positions shift by a few pixels, and neither change makes one better than the other.

Both fail the same ways. The headline sits on the busy hand and bottle photo, so 'Drink Water' and 'Should You' collide with the fingers. The zigzag ornaments overlap 'During', and the yellow ribbon tails are cut off from the 'a Workout?' band, which floats far below them as a separate piece. A is slightly worse because its stack is more spread out: the top dotted rule cuts across the finger and the gap between the ribbon tails and the band is bigger. B's text block is a little tighter, but it is still broken.

The two candidates use the same weak layout. In both, the light-blue highlight behind 'HOUSE' has broken away and floats as a stray bar near the top. The pillow photo, the key image, is shrunk to a small strip in the middle, the headline sits almost against the left edge, the body copy is nearly as big as the headline, and the contact box is left floating above a large empty area at the bottom. B places the content a little lower, which balances the vertical space slightly better than A's top-heavy stack, but A has less dead space between the copy and the photo, so the difference is marginal.

Both lose the original's full-bleed pizza background. The photo shrinks to a small, washed-out thumbnail sitting loose on white, with no link to the orange headline band, and the headline wraps into choppy lines with 'to' orphaned on its own line. A pushes the band near the top and leaves about 200px of empty white at the bottom, so it is badly lopsided; B is the same layout but centred vertically, so its empty space is more evenly spread, which makes it marginally less unbalanced.

Both are weak. Each shrinks the house photo into a small tile, and the pool image becomes a tiny scrap stuck between beige blocks at the bottom. Both leave large dead white gaps around a small headline that does not fill the width. A spreads these pieces a little more evenly down the canvas. B pushes everything down, leaving a big empty top, and jams the pool scrap and beige blocks against the bottom edge, so its balance is worse.

Both break the original the same way. The frame outline that should surround the headline floats empty near the top, a grey panel and the bulb icon are grouped as a stray cluster under the text, and the leaf imagery is reduced to a blur at the top edge, so most of the eco feel is lost. A is worse because the grey panel and icon sit jammed against the bottom edge and the headline sits low, leaving the upper half empty. B gives that bottom group a margin and spaces things more evenly, so it reads slightly better.

The two are almost identical and both are broken. The leafy photo is reduced to a green blob at the top. The frame is now an empty box floating mid-canvas. The bulb icon and divider lines are pushed to the bottom and sit against a grey bar. The headline's first line runs nearly edge to edge with no side margin, and there are large dead areas. A is slightly less bad because its headline has more breathing room below the top blob, while B's headline is jammed against the top.

Both candidates are close to identical, and both break the design the same way. The headline has been pulled out of its search bar, so the white search bar now sits empty and meaningless at the top. The CTA button's text is too small to read, the 'Д.' in the 'ОНЛАЙН-КУРС Д. СИЛАНТЬЕВА' line is left alone on its own line, and the laptops, glasses and black ring are cropped into unrecognisable scraps (a half ring and a black blob at the bottom). B wins by a very small margin because its search bar sits lower with a little more top margin, while A's is jammed almost against the top edge.

Both candidates have the same flaws. The olive panel behind the headline is gone, so the brand colour survives only as two small olive boxes near the bottom that don't mean anything. The '- SOREN KIERKEGAARD' credit is set almost as big and bold as the quote, which flattens the hierarchy. The white outline frame floats over the church with no link to the text. The only real difference is position: A sits lower, with more empty space at the top and the olive boxes almost touching the bottom edge, while B sits higher and crowds the frame up against the credit line.

A and B are almost pixel-identical and share the same flaws. The 'STATIONERY SALE' headline is set far too small for the canvas, so the pen row overpowers it, and there is a large dead red gap between the pens and the headline and another below it. The 11th pencil is stranded as a tiny orphan in the bottom-left corner instead of staying with its group. The only difference is that B's pen row sits a few pixels lower and its headline slightly higher, which changes nothing.

The two layouts are practically the same: the row of pens sits above a centred 'STATIONERY SALE' headline. In both, the lone pencil that ended the original banner floats off to the right below the text and lines up with nothing, and the bottom ~40% of the canvas is empty red, so the composition is top-heavy and looks unfinished. B sits only a few pixels higher than A, which changes nothing, and neither one rebuilds the original pen-row-into-headline rhythm with any intent.

Both are almost the same crop of the wrapped hand, and that crop drops the torso and arm that give the original its power. Both also leave the LUST/FOR/WIN lockup small and pushed nearly to the side edges of the narrow canvas, with the letter-spaced WIN running close to both sides. A's LUST runs almost to the right edge and its dotted rule sits farther below WIN than in the original. B keeps the dot row tight under WIN as the original does and centres the lockup slightly better, so it edges ahead.

I can't see any difference between the two. Both drop the misty crane photo, which is half of the original's imagery. In both, the pink brush stroke has come off the headline: it floats as a separate bar above it instead of underlining it. Both also leave a stray brush fragment at the bottom edge. The body copy sits close under the headline, and the brick photo becomes a narrow pillar with wide empty side margins and an unbalanced bottom.

A: the white rule cuts straight through '2018' and runs into the 'Tickets are available' line. The bag logo is blown up oversized and pushed against the bottom edge, and the dot pattern has been squashed into a strip that runs off the canvas. The photo, the key image, is cut down to an unreadable sliver at the right edge. B: keeps the original structure, colours and logo with no collisions. Its flaws are the small headline and date, which leave lots of empty red space, the tiny low-weight tagline, and an added left photo panel that splits the composition and competes with the red block.

The two are almost the same: the red panel is a cramped box in the top half, and the photo below fills more than half the canvas with a visible translucent ghost rectangle over the middle. The 'Tickets are available' line and the date are tiny at this size. A floats the panel and dot grid about 15px below the top edge, leaving a thin, odd strip of photo above them; B keeps the panel flush to the top like the original's full-height panel, so it reads slightly more intentionally.

A and B are nearly the same layout; B just sits about 15–25 px lower. In both, the text stack is misaligned: 'JULY 29' and its divider are pushed right while 'SEWING CLASS' and 'FOR BEGINNERS' are roughly centred. 'FOR BEGINNERS' is jammed against the safety pins, the illustration is shrunk to a small cluster, and the top and bottom of the canvas are left as large dead bands while the GROVE.ONLINE ribbon floats on its own. Neither one is clearly better.

Both use the same weak layout. The headline has shrunk to a small size, with a huge dead gap between 'CHILDREN'S' and 'DAY', so the title no longer reads as one unit. Lots of yellow space is wasted, the address is tiny, and confetti sits on top of the train (the blue dash and green dot). In B the date and address have slid down, and the first '1' of the address looks clipped or hidden ('2231'), so A is slightly better.

Both candidates use the same broken layout. The address is crushed into a tiny 3-line column ('4275 / Country / Club Dr') beside the date. The second model photo is cut off from the composition and floats below the pattern block, off-centre to the left, with her head cropped and unrelated dead white space on its right. The seated-model photo has also lost its pattern-block framing. B sits slightly lower on the canvas, so its top and bottom margins are a little more even than A's (A has a cramped top and a large empty band at the bottom). That small difference is the only edge.

Both crop the model's face down to one eye on the edge and let the huge blue panel cover most of the image. Both leave the thin outline frame floating in the foliage, detached from the panel, and move the '14' beside the text column, which breaks the original's centred stacked reading order. A crams the text column against the top of the panel and leaves a dead blue band about 95px tall at the bottom; B spaces the content more evenly down the panel, so it is slightly less lopsided.

A and B are almost the same layout, and both have the same problems. The 'NEW YORK' ribbon is much larger than the 'SUBWAY' and 'GUIDE' ribbons, which breaks the original's evenly sized three-line title stack. The gaps between the ribbons are uneven. The diagonal stripe graphics have broken into floating grey and beige shapes that sit on top of the photo at the lower right. A faint translucent shape also collides with the 'SUB' lettering at the lower left. A has slightly tighter ribbon spacing and B has slightly looser spacing, but neither one is better than the other.

Both use the same weak layout. The equal-width title bars from the original have become one oversized NEW YORK bar above two stubby SUBWAY and GUIDE bars, so the key word SUBWAY is demoted. NEW YORK's text is also indented further than the other two lines. The photo is cropped so the sign reads 'BWAY', and the diagonal grey/beige panels have broken into floating fragments with faint ghost shapes on the left. A pushes the title stack tight against the top edge and leaves the fragments hanging awkwardly mid-canvas. B gives the title a little more top margin and sits the fragments lower, so it is slightly less awkward.

Both crop the crucifix badly: the left arm is cut off and the corpus is pushed against the left edge. Both also break the original's thin border frame, which ends up as a stray rectangle floating over the cross arm in the upper half instead of outlining the canvas. A also leaves a loose gap between 'Easter' and 'CHURCH SERVICE', with dead space above them. B is nearly identical but keeps the two text lines more tightly grouped as one lockup, which makes it slightly better despite sitting a bit lower on the canvas.

Both have the same broken layout. The photo is shrunk to a small thumbnail and pushed against the right edge, with pink corner triangles blown up over the model's face. The three label bars are right-aligned and spaced unevenly (the gap before 'Photography' is much larger), and a huge empty black area runs down the left side and the middle. B is the same layout moved up, which leaves about 200px of dead black at the bottom. A sits slightly more centred vertically, so it is marginally less lopsided.

The two candidates look pixel-identical. Both have the same failures: the 'FUN GROUP' brand text is blown up so it is almost as big as the headline, and it sits right on top of the busy bike and bunny watercolour, which is a collision and hurts legibility. The bunny-on-bike illustration is cropped on both sides, so the basket and wheels are cut off. A leaf sprig is clipped at the right edge. The small headline floats over a large empty band at the top.

I couldn't see any difference between the two candidates. Both keep the original's three-column header row unchanged but shrink it, so the tagline, address and 'Since 1982' text become tiny. Both leave a band of empty sky above the header, and the headline line 'a daring adventure or' runs almost to both canvas edges. The tall format isn't really used: the layout is the original, scaled down and cropped, rather than rearranged.

Both candidates are unusable in nearly the same way. The quote 'Dogs never bite me — just humans.' and the 'Marilyn Monroe' attribution are gone. The teal photo background has dropped out, leaving a mostly empty white frame. The teal panel, the dog photo and the icon sprites are piled in a clump below the frame. Only the frame outline, a few stray icons and a faint divider line are left. A's divider is slightly more visible, but that makes no real difference.

Both keep the headline, chevron and nurse illustration in their original order with correct colours. Neither rearranges the layout; each is a straight scale onto the taller 1:2 canvas. In A, the illustration's cropped bottom edge stops about 35px above the canvas bottom. That leaves a band of purple under the figure, which loses the original's bleed-off-the-edge look and makes the figure seem to float. B has the same fault, but its band is smaller and the chevron spacing is slightly better, so B is a little better.

Both make the same mistakes. The pattern frame is left as an empty hole, and the headline 'WE LOVE YOU!' is pulled out of the frame and shrunk into a small, cramped text stack under it. The reading order is also jumbled: 'DEAR TEACHERS!' now sits below the headline and the school name, which breaks the original greeting → message → details flow. The only difference is placement: A pushes everything up and leaves about 130px of dead space at the bottom, while B centres the group a little better vertically, so B is slightly more balanced.

The two candidates are almost identical and both fail in the same ways. The hero photo is shrunk to a small strip floating in white space, with a large dead gap between it and the headline. The headline has lost its yellow underline bars and no longer overlaps the image. The big circle is cut off at the top, the circle motif is shrunk to a tiny dot cluster, and the yellow bars are scattered at the bottom with no link to the text. B's headline leading is slightly tighter, closer to the original, but its dot cluster looks clipped, so neither one is better overall.

Both are cropped crude zooms of the photo with black headline text placed straight onto the busy hand and finger, so the copy is hard to read. Both also break the yellow ribbon apart: the tails float at mid-height and are detached from the 'a Workout?' bar, and the dotted rules cut across the finger. A is slightly less bad because its bar sits closer to the ribbon tails and the text stack is a bit tighter; B pushes the bar even further below the tails, which makes the broken ribbon more obvious.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both have the same flaws. The pillow photo has shrunk to a small strip, so the hero image no longer matters. The light-blue highlight behind 'HOUSE' is gone, and two pale blue bars sit loose at the top with no purpose. The body copy is nearly as big as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy. There are big dead gaps between the text, the photo and the contact box, and the space under the contact box is empty. A edges ahead only because its stack sits a little lower, leaving less empty space at the bottom than B, which is pushed up and more bottom-heavy in empty space.

Both throw away the original's full-bleed pizza photo. Each shrinks it to a small thumbnail floating on a plain white background, separate from the orange band, and both break the headline over five lines with 'to' alone on its own line. A centres the group a little better. B pushes the band near the top and leaves about 200px of empty white at the bottom, so its balance is worse.

A: The house photo is shrunk to a small thumbnail with large dead white gaps above and below it. The title floats in mid-canvas, and the pool photo and beige accent blocks are squeezed into a fragmented strip that jams against the bottom edge. B: It makes the same mistakes: a small photo, the same small title, and long empty stretches. The bottom cluster is also scattered, with the beige block hanging off on its own at the lower right. Its vertical spacing is a little more even, which makes it slightly less broken than A.

Both lose the original's main structure. The thin frame that surrounded the headline is now an empty box floating above the text, a stray grey rectangle sits next to the icon, the leaf imagery is almost gone, and the bulb icon and divider lines are pushed off into a bottom corner. B has all the same flaws and is also shifted down, so the grey block, icon and lines are jammed against the bottom edge with no margin; that makes A slightly less bad.

Both break the original the same way. The white frame that framed the headline is now an empty box floating mid-canvas, the leaf imagery is reduced to a blurry blob at the top, and the bulb icon and divider are stranded at the bottom next to a meaningless grey bar. The 'ECO-CONSCIOUSNESS.' line runs almost edge to edge, and there is a large dead area between the frame and the bottom. A's headline is jammed near the top edge. B's headline sits lower and breathes slightly better, but B's bottom icon cluster is pressed against the bottom edge, so B is only marginally less bad.

Both break the search-bar concept the same way: the white pill sits empty at the top with no search icon, and the headline is pulled out of it. Both CTA buttons are shrunk until the text can't be read, the laptops and camera are gone, leaving a cropped glasses fragment and a stray black ring, and both have dead gray space between the subcopy and the CTA. B's headline is larger and 'identity' nearly touches the right edge; A keeps slightly better side margins, so it is marginally less broken.

The two candidates are nearly identical, and both lose the brand: the olive block behind the headline is gone, and the olive panels are reduced to two small, meaningless rectangles at the bottom. Both also set the attribution in bold at almost the headline's size, so the hierarchy is weak, and the thin white frame floats over the steeple with no clear purpose. A is slightly better balanced. B leaves extra dead space at the top and pushes its olive rectangles almost against the bottom edge.

The two layouts are almost identical. In both, the 'STATIONERY SALE' headline is too small and gets lost in a large empty red field, and the pen row is the main focal point instead of the message. A lone pencil also sits stranded in the bottom-left corner, cut off from the group of pens. That leaves big dead gaps above the pens, between pens and headline, and below. B's pens are slightly larger and its headline sits slightly lower, but the difference is negligible.

A and B are effectively the same layout. B sits only a few pixels lower, so its block is marginally closer to vertical centre. Both stack the pen row above a centred two-line 'STATIONERY SALE' headline, which reads fine. Both share the same flaws: the lone pencil floats at lower right with no relationship to the headline or the pen row, the bottom third of the canvas is empty red, and nothing is scaled up for the tall format.

A and B are practically the same, differing by only a few pixels of vertical offset. Both shrink the square original into the middle of the portrait canvas without rearranging anything. They both leave lighter, mismatched texture bands across the top and bottom, which looks like a letterbox. The bracket frame and fabric photo don't use the extra height, and the small subtitle, date and address text gets even smaller.

Both are tiny shrunken copies of the square layout centred in a wide banner. Large empty white bands sit on either side, and the headline and body copy are illegible at this size, so neither is rearranged for the banner format. B is a little worse because a stray dark striped block (probably the brush stroke that was meant to sit under the headline) is floating loose between the text and the crane photo, which adds a visible collision and grouping error.

Both fail in the same ways. The brick and crane photos have shrunk to tiny thumbnails, so the original's key imagery is effectively gone. The pink brush underline has come away from the headline, been duplicated and been stretched into stray bars. The headline and body copy are tiny on a mostly empty white column with large dead areas. Their layouts are nearly the same: A places the text block slightly higher and B slightly lower, but neither is better.

Both candidates break apart the layered polaroid group. The grey mat, the white frame and the stamp circle end up side by side in a small row at the top, and the torn-paper edge becomes a floating white sliver in the middle. That destroys the design's intent and leaves no clear focal image. The headline is now the most prominent element, oversized and pushed to the bottom. A and B differ only by a few pixels of vertical spacing (B's top row sits slightly closer to the top edge, and A's text sits slightly closer to the bottom edge), so neither one is better.

The two layouts are nearly identical, and they share the same flaws. The 'JULY 29' date is shrunk into a small side label next to the huge headline, so it loses its role as a clear tier above it. The red divider is left on its own at the far left. The sewing illustration is pushed left, leaving a large empty area on the right. B narrows A's top margin and moves the illustration up, so its gap to the 'FOR BEGINNERS / GROVE.ONLINE' footer is less cramped than in A, but the difference is small.

The two are almost identical: in both, 'JULY 29' is crammed into a tiny two-line stack beside the headline, so it loses its role as a lead-in, and the short red divider floats alone with nothing near it. A also leaves a large dead gap between the headline and the illustration while the headline sits close to the top. B moves the whole block down, which spreads the space more evenly, but it pushes the illustration close to the 'FOR BEGINNERS'/GROVE.ONLINE footer row.

Both look like the landscape layout pushed into a tall frame. The type block is tiny and stuck in the right column, and there are big empty gaps between 'International', 'CHILDREN'S' and 'DAY', so the headline doesn't read as one unit. The cropped bricks and train crowd the left side and the bottom. In B, the address line also slides under the red train's wheel, so '1223…' is hidden. A's address is just as tiny but stays clear of the train, so A is slightly less broken.

Both use the same weak stacked layout. The yellow blocks sit awkwardly over the top-right of the hero photo. The second photo is jammed into the left of a large, mostly empty yellow slab. The 'Online training by' and 'Freya Anouk' labels are tiny, low in the hierarchy, and float off-axis from the left-aligned headline. B is slightly worse: its black accent bar runs straight into the 'Online training by' label. A leaves a small gap there, but 'Freya Anouk' sits close to the bottom edge.

A leaves an empty white strip across the top. 'BEST TRX' crowds the bottom edge of the photo, 'EXERCISES' runs into the yellow bar, and 'FREYA ANOUK' sits about 140px below 'ONLINE TRAINING BY', so the byline falls apart. B is cleaner: the photo runs to the top and the headline sits clear below it with no collisions. Both still have the same core flaws: the yellow headline backing bars are left floating on the photo, the byline pills are far apart, the lower left is a large dead white area, and the bottom half reads as an unfinished stack rather than a rearranged design.

Both use the same broken layout. Yellow blocks sit across the woman photo, the second photo has shrunk to an unreadable sliver, and 'FREYA ANOUK' is split off above the headline while 'ONLINE TRAINING BY' is stranded at the bottom, so the credit line reads in the wrong order. Both also lose the full-bleed photo and leave large white dead zones between pieces of text. A is slightly less bad because its photo is a bit larger and the gaps between elements are a little less extreme; B's photo is smaller and its empty space is worse.

Both use the same broken layout. The address is squeezed into a cramped 3-line '4275 / Country / Club Dr' column beside the date, and 'keaton.us' is too small to read. The large model photo floats as a separate block below the pattern panel and is not right-aligned with it, which leaves a dead white strip on the right. The model's head is also cropped at the top. A spaces things a bit more evenly from top to bottom, with similar top and bottom margins and a taller photo. B is pushed up and leaves a large empty area at the bottom.

The two layouts are nearly identical, so this is a tie. Both have the same problems: the top ~180px and bottom ~120px of the skyscraper are left empty, and the bottom bracket mark is blown up, blurry and much larger than the top one, so it looks distorted. 'LEARNING' runs almost to the right edge, and the photo is cropped hard against the left edge, so the content is jammed into the middle band. B leaves slightly more space under its slightly shorter photo, while A's photo is a touch larger. Neither difference changes the score.

Both crop the photo so only a thin, unreadable sliver of the woman's face shows at the right edge, which loses the key image, and both shrink the blue panel's small text (Online Workshop, FREE JOIN) to near-illegible sizes. A sits the panel a little above centre, leaving a reasonable strip of foliage below it. B pushes its panel down until it almost touches the bottom edge, which leaves dead foliage above and a cramped bottom margin.

Both break the original the same way. 'NEW YORK' has lost its navy ribbon and now sits as bare white serif text on the busy photo. An empty navy stub floats above it, the 'SUBWAY' and 'GUIDE' ribbons are tiny next to it, and the grey diagonal panels have broken into stray fragments. A also leaves a dead band of photo above the title group, and its fragments look like glitches near the bottom. B anchors the title block at the top, which reads better for a tall skyscraper banner, but it crowds the empty bar against the title and leaves the same stray shards mid-canvas, so it is only slightly less bad.

Both use the same broken layout. The checkmarks sit stacked under the headline, but their list labels ('Legs / Chin Upper lip Ears / Chest Bikini Area') have been moved to the bottom right as tiny, illegible text with nothing next to them. The $50 sits off to the right of the divider line, separated from 'ONE DAY ONLY TO SAVE', which has dropped below MUSELIO.PT, so the reading order is jumbled. Tape fragments are scattered at the bottom, the white card and spa photo are lost or shrunk, and there are large dead gaps. B only shifts everything up slightly and crops the photo a little differently, so the two are effectively the same.

Both use almost the same crop, which cuts the crucifix figure down to a single arm and a sliver of the post. That loses the original's key image, and the thin inset frame border is gone too. In both, the left edge of 'Easter' presses against the cross post. B leaves a large, loose gap between 'Easter' and 'CHURCH SERVICE', so the headline and subtitle stop reading as one block. A keeps them closer together, which is slightly better grouping, though the pair sits low with dead dark space above.

Both use the same bad crop of the photo: the cross and crucifix, which are the key image, are cut down to an unreadable fragment of a hand and a strip of wood. The thin frame border is also gone, so neither still reads as the same Easter design. Both put 'Easter' and 'CHURCH SERVICE' in the lower middle with nearly identical type. 'Easter' runs almost edge to edge in A and has very slightly more side margin in B. Apart from that they are effectively the same.

Both fail in the same ways. The photo has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail pushed to the right edge, and a pink corner triangle cuts across the model's face. The text bars are in the wrong order, with Photography first and LomoArt second, so the 'LomoArt Fashion Photography' brand line is jumbled. Large black dead areas surround a small, scattered cluster of content. B gets the slight edge only because its content sits closer to the vertical centre; A leaves about 215px of empty black at the bottom.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both share the same flaws. The 'Biggest Plants' headline is tiny for a story format, and 'WORLD'S' is not aligned with the headline. The dotted arc almost touches 'WORLD'S'. The horizontal rule and the dot rows float with no purpose, and there are large empty areas on the right side and at the bottom. A is slightly worse because its stack sits high: the top image is jammed under the black bar and the bottom has more dead space. B shifts everything down a little, which gives a more even vertical balance.

A keeps the original structure: the headline, divider, subhead and chevron are spaced the same way in the panel. Its main flaw is one it inherits from the original: 'YOU WANT' pushes right up to the panel's right edge. B has a clear collision: the divider rule cuts across the baseline of 'YOU' in the headline. It also leaves a large dead gap before the subhead, which makes the panel's spacing uneven.

The two are almost identical. Both keep the ram skull, the yellow bar and the quote faithfully, but they stack everything in the top 85% and leave a large empty band at the bottom of the tall canvas. The attribution also sits a couple of pixels left of the quote's left edge. The only difference is the attribution's spacing. A leaves a wider gap under the quote, so the credit looks detached. B keeps it tighter, closer to the original's grouping.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical: both just scale the original block up and drop it into the taller canvas instead of rearranging it, which leaves a big empty band (about 100 px) at the top and another at the bottom. The info line runs nearly to the right edge in both, and the 'GALLERY|' divider sits right against the Y. Neither uses the story format: the headline stays small, the artwork is not enlarged to fill the frame, and there is no top-to-bottom flow. The only difference is a few pixels in where the artwork sits vertically, so I can't pick one over the other.

A and B look pixel-identical, so this is a tie. Both keep the brand, the hierarchy and the illustration intact, but they scale the whole stack down and push it toward the top. That leaves a large empty band of about 100px below the #FlattenTheCurve/#StayAtHome hashtags, so the layout feels top-heavy. The small kicker text and hashtags also get quite small at this size, and the phone illustrations sit close to the side edges.

A and B are almost pixel-for-pixel the same: the original layout is shrunk and centred in the tall canvas. In both, the top title and the date/school lines are tiny, and roughly 130px of empty navy sits above and below the content. Nothing was rearranged to use the taller story format. B sits a few pixels higher and leaves slightly more space under the frame, which is not enough to separate them.

Both use the same weak layout. The light-blue highlight bar has come loose from 'HOUSE' and floats as a stray rectangle above the headline. The subtitle sits jammed against the headline and breaks badly, leaving 'towels,' alone on its own line. The pillow photo, the original's main visual, has shrunk to a small strip, and the bottom quarter of the canvas is empty. B is slightly better: it sits a little lower, which shrinks the empty bottom area, but the difference is minor.

Both drop the original's full-bleed pizza photo with an overlaid band. Instead they stack a full-width orange headline band above a small inset photo, which leaves large empty white areas and loses the feel of the original. The inset photo also doesn't line up with the edge-to-edge band. A keeps the band and photo group closer to vertical centre (about 97px of white above, 125px below). B pushes the group up, leaving about 160px of dead white space at the bottom, so it is more lopsided.

The two are nearly identical and share the same problems. The full-bleed pizza photo has been reduced to a small inset with a white border, and the orange headline band is now a separate strip floating in empty white space, so it no longer crosses the image. That loses the original's layered, immersive look and leaves large dead areas above, between and below. B sits about 20px lower, which evens out the top and bottom white space a little (A has roughly 140px at the top and 200px at the bottom), so B is marginally less lopsided.

The two candidates are almost the same, and both are broken. Each drops the full-bleed pizza background, leaving a small photo and a thin orange headline band floating on plain white. Roughly half the tall canvas is empty white space (at the top, between the band and the photo, and at the bottom), and the headline is small for the format. The band no longer overlaps the image, so the original's layered feel is gone. A is slightly better balanced vertically, with about 170px of white above and 183px below, while B sits higher with about 150px above and 200px below. B is no better in any other way.

Both are the same weak layout. The photo stays as a small block in the top-left, and the headline and subhead are pushed right: they start at x≈165 while the photo starts at x≈58, and the text runs past the photo's right edge, so the two share no common edge. Below the subhead there is a large dead area, and the decorative dots look scattered. A sits slightly lower, so the content block is a little better centred (≈230px of empty space at the bottom vs ≈270px in B), which makes it marginally less top-heavy. Neither is rearranged with intent for the near-square format.

Both candidates have nearly the same layout and the same flaws. The left arrow ornament is stretched into a blurry smear, and the light-blue side strip stops abruptly halfway down. The illustration runs off the right edge. 'YOUR EFFICIENT' is split far away from 'ENERGY USE' by a large dead gap, and the bottom third is empty, so the headline floats with no grouping. B's headline is slightly larger, but it doesn't fix any of these problems.

Both break the original's key idea, a search bar with the headline typed inside it. The white pill is left empty, the black search button is blown up into a huge block cut off at the right edge, and the headline sits outside the bar. All the laptop, notebook and phone imagery is gone, leaving cropped arcs as dead decoration. The secondary line 'ОНЛАЙН-КУРС Д. СИЛАНТЬЕВА' is now almost as big as the headline, so the two compete. The two are nearly identical. B is slightly worse because its subtitle is jammed against the CTA button and its stack sits lower with less breathing room, while A spaces the subtitle and CTA a bit more evenly.

A and B are almost the same layout. In both, the pen row floats with a large dead band above it and another between it and the headline. The headline 'STATIONERY SALE' runs to within about 12px of the side edges, and the lone pencil left over from the original's right edge is stranded at the bottom-left corner, cut off from the group. B sits slightly lower, so the vertical spacing is a little more even, but neither one deals with the empty space or the stray pencil.

Both are the same uniformly shrunk copy of the square original. The grey background panel doesn't reach the top or bottom of the canvas, which leaves mismatched lighter textured bands (about 75px each) that look like a rendering error. Nothing has been re-laid out for the taller format. The text is smaller than in the original, and the event line and address are now small. B only sits a few pixels lower than A, so they're effectively identical.

Both are a shrunken copy of the square design sitting in the middle of an extreme wide banner. Roughly 80% of the canvas is left as empty white on either side. The headline and body copy are tiny and can't be read, and nothing was rearranged to read left to right. A looks slightly worse because its text block seems to have a stray pinkish element (probably the brush stroke) sitting below the body copy. In B the stroke stays under the headline, but B is still unusable.

Both fail in the same ways. The brick and crane photos shrink to small thumbnails stuck at the left edge. The pink brush stroke that sat under the headline is detached and repeated as two loose bars further down. The headline and body text are tiny and float in a huge white space with large gaps between them. Neither candidate is ship-ready, and the small vertical shifts between them make no real difference.

Both break apart the original's layered polaroid composition: the grey mat, the white frame and the circular stamp sit in a row of small, disconnected thumbnails across the top, and the torn-paper edge has become an isolated white shard floating in the middle. The caption, originally inside the frame, is now a large headline cut off from the frame, so the design's main idea is lost and the empty centre wastes most of the canvas. The two are nearly identical; B shifts everything down, which leaves the headline almost touching the bottom edge, so A is very slightly less cramped.

A and B share the same layout and differ only in a vertical shift of about 20px. Both have the same flaws: the divider is orphaned at the left, red, and no longer tied to the date. 'JULY 29' is shrunk to a small side-note wrapped onto two lines. The illustration cluster is crammed into the lower-left, leaving a dead right half. 'FOR BEGINNERS' and the GROVE.ONLINE ribbon are pushed against the bottom edge. Neither candidate is clearly better.

The two are almost the same layout. In both, 'JULY 29' has shrunk to a tiny stacked label next to the headline, so the date loses its role. The red divider floats on its own at the left in a large empty band between the headline and the illustration. The footer row ('FOR BEGINNERS' and the GROVE.ONLINE ribbon) also sits apart from the headline group. A pushes everything lower, leaving a large top margin and the footer jammed near the bottom edge. B's vertical spacing is slightly more even, but its gap between the headline and the illustration is still a dead area.

Both are weak, stretched copies of the original. The text column is pushed right of centre and the headline is tiny, so 'CHILDREN'S' and 'DAY' no longer dominate the poster, and the big gaps between headline lines read as disconnected fragments. The cropped lego pieces sit along the left edge as dead weight, and the logo and address are illegibly small. In A, the address line also collides with the red train, which covers its start ('12231 S'). B keeps the address clear of the train and groups the date and address slightly more tightly, so B is a bit less bad.

Both use the same weak stacked layout. The yellow blocks sit on top of the photo of the woman and hide part of it. The headline has lost its yellow backing and floats on plain white. The second photo is jammed into the left side of a large, empty yellow box, and the white spaces around it look unplanned. In the original, the 'ONLINE TRAINING BY' and 'FREYA ANOUK' labels sat together; here they are split apart. In B the gap between them is wider and 'FREYA ANOUK' is pushed against the bottom edge. A's slightly tighter grouping makes it marginally less bad, though its small black bar nearly touches the upper label.

A: the yellow accent bars float over the photo, cut off from the headline. The 'Online training by' and 'Freya Anouk' labels are split by a big empty gap beside a tall yellow bar. The lower-left half of the canvas is dead white, so the layout reads as a collage that fell apart. B has the same broken lower half and also adds an empty white strip above the photo. Its 'BEST TRX' crowds the bottom edge of the photo, the tall bar overlaps 'SES' of the headline, and 'FREYA ANOUK' is jammed near the bottom edge, so B is slightly worse.

Both use the same broken layout. Hierarchy and reading order are wrong: 'FREYA ANOUK' sits far above the headline, while 'ONLINE TRAINING BY' is stranded near the bottom, so the byline reads backwards. The yellow frame blocks are pasted over the hero photo. The second photo has shrunk to an unreadable sliver, and huge dead white gaps separate the scattered pieces. The original's full-bleed photo and yellow-block identity are lost. B has a slightly more balanced top margin; A's photo is jammed near the top, which leaves even more lopsided emptiness. Otherwise they are equivalent.

The two layouts are almost identical and share the same serious flaws. The address is squeezed into a cramped, tiny three-line stack ('4275 / Country / Club Dr') beside the date. 'keaton.us' and 'SHOWROOM' are too small to read. The second photo is left-aligned and stops well short of the right edge, so it looks disconnected from the patterned panel and leaves a lopsided gap on the right. A adds a large dead white area at the bottom with only a thin top margin. B shifts everything down so the empty space above and below is more even, which makes it slightly less unbalanced.

A and B are nearly the same layout and share the same faults. The bottom bracket mark is blown up to many times the size of the top one and looks blurred and distorted. The photo is cropped small and runs off the left edge, and its frame line floats away from it. 'PLAYFUL LEARNING' nearly touches the right edge. The whole group sits in a narrow middle band, leaving large dead areas at the top and bottom. The only difference is that B's photo and text sit a few pixels lower; neither one is ship-ready.

Both crop the model's face to a half-sliver on the right edge, so the hero image and the original's balance are largely lost. The blue panel nearly fills the width and pushes the face off the edge. The panel's small text (Online Workshop, FREE JOIN) is also tiny in a 160px column. A sits its panel lower, so the eye, nose and lips stay visible, although its bottom margin is tight. B raises the panel so its right edge covers the lips, which hides even more of the face; B's only edge is a more centred vertical position.

Both break the original's banded-ribbon title: 'NEW YORK' is pulled out of its navy ribbon and set loose on the busy photo, an empty navy bar sits above it, the SUBWAY/GUIDE ribbons are shrunk to small secondary chips, and the grey diagonal stripes are left as stray fragments mid-canvas, with the bottom 60% just cropped photo. A sits higher, its white headline is on a darker part of the photo, and it reads a little more cleanly. B pushes the title down onto lighter, busier sign lettering, which weakens contrast and leaves a muddier top area.

Both have the same layout breakdown. The six checkmarks sit in an empty column with no labels, and the list items they belong to (Legs, Chin Upper lip, Ears…) are moved to the bottom right in tiny, unreadable text. The tape pieces are scattered at the bottom as loose debris, and the white note card is gone. The $50 floats beside a stray blue rule, and 'One day only to save' sits under the photo, away from the price it explains, so the reading order is jumbled. B's slightly lower placement and larger photo make no real difference.

Both use the same bad crop of the background: the crucifix, which is the main image, is cut down to a sliver of wood and one silver arm at the left edge. The original's thin frame border is gone, and 'Easter' sits right against the cross upright with almost no left margin. A leaves a large, loose gap between 'Easter' and 'CHURCH SERVICE', so the title and its subtitle don't read as one block. B moves the headline down and groups the two lines more tightly, which makes it slightly better, though it is still not shippable.

A and B are almost pixel-identical, and both are broken the same way. Each crops the background to a blurry piece of the cross arm with a single metal hand, so the crucifix, which is the key image, is gone and the top third is dead dark space. 'Easter' is stretched almost edge to edge with almost no side margin, the thin frame line from the original is missing, and the text block sits low with no clear intent.

Both are essentially the same failed layout. The photo is shrunk to a thumbnail and pushed against the right edge, and the pink corner triangles are scaled up until they cover the model. The label order is scrambled to Photography/LomoArt/Fashion, so the LomoArt brand name is no longer on top. Huge black dead zones fill the rest of the tall canvas. A is very slightly better balanced from top to bottom. B sits higher and leaves a bigger empty area at the bottom, but the difference is marginal.

The two layouts are almost identical. In both, the 'Biggest Plants' headline is too small for a tall story format. A big white area sits to the right of the top image, the rule line and dot clusters float with no purpose, and 'WORLD'S' is separated from the headline. B moves everything up, which leaves an even bigger blank band at the bottom (about 90px) and a lopsided layout. A spreads the vertical space a little more evenly, but it has its own awkward gap under the top black bar.

A: the divider rule runs into the headline. It sits right under 'YOU' and reads like an accidental underline. There is also a wide dead gap above 'NOT FOR THE ONE YOU HAVE', which pulls the subhead away from the headline it belongs with. B keeps the original's order and spacing (headline, rule, subhead, then the chevron panel) with even gaps. As in the original, the headline still runs past the right edge of the panel, and the subhead is small at 300px wide, so B needs only minor polish.

The two candidates are almost identical, and both have the same flaws. The ram skull and yellow bar keep their proportions, but the whole layout is pushed up, leaving about 120px of dead white space at the bottom. The small attribution line also sits a couple of pixels left of the quote's left edge. The only difference is where the attribution sits. In A it is a bit tight under the quote, about the same relative gap as the original. In B the gap is wider and the attribution looks slightly detached. Neither difference matters enough to pick a winner.

Both are the same mechanical scale-down of the original into a tall canvas. Each leaves about 100px of empty space at the top and about 90px at the bottom, keeps the small headline and the tiny letter-spaced info line (which still runs nearly to the right edge), and does not rearrange anything for the story format. A is marginally better because it leaves a little more space between the info line and the halftone image. In B the image almost touches the info line, which makes that part feel cramped.

A and B look pixel-identical. Both are a uniform shrink of the 9:16 original into the taller 1:2 canvas, not a rearrangement. That leaves about 100px of dead white space below the hashtags, against tighter top spacing, so the layout looks bottom-empty and is not adapted to the format. The hashtags and the 'WE'LL GET THROUGH' kicker are also small at this size. Hierarchy, colours, illustration proportions and the absence of collisions are all preserved.

Both are near-identical shrink-and-center versions. The doodle frame is scaled into the narrow width, which leaves large dead navy bands above the title (~130px) and below the school name (~130px), and the 'National Teacher Appreciation Day' and footer lines are now small and thin for a story format. A spaces the title-to-frame and frame-to-date gaps evenly (~58px each). B sits the frame a little lower, so the footer gap is tighter (~51px) and the date-to-school gap is cramped, which makes it slightly less balanced.

Both use the same layout with the same flaws. The light-blue highlight bar has come loose from 'HOUSE' and floats as a meaningless stripe. The subtitle sits jammed against the headline and breaks badly, leaving 'towels,' alone on its own line. The hero photo of the pillows has shrunk to a small strip, and a large empty band is left at the bottom. B is shifted further up, so its bottom gap is even bigger and it looks more top-heavy; A is spread slightly more evenly down the canvas.

Both candidates have the same flaw: the full-bleed pizza photo with the orange band across it has been turned into a plain white page. The full-width band sits on top of a small inset photo with ~22px side margins that don't line up with the band, and there is a large blank white area at the bottom, so the original's bold immersive feel is lost. A is worse because the stack sits high (~63px gap at the top versus ~160px of empty white at the bottom). B is more evenly centred (~97px top, ~125px bottom), but it still leaves dead space and has the same mismatched edges.

Both make the same mistakes. The full-bleed pizza photo, which was the original's background, is now a small inset rectangle floating on white. The orange headline band sits about 70px above the photo instead of crossing it, so the layered look is gone. That leaves large empty white areas at the top and bottom, and the result looks like stacked pieces rather than a recomposed design. A's content block sits slightly closer to the vertical centre (about 160px of white above, 180px below). B is shifted up about 20px, which leaves more dead space at the bottom, so A is marginally less lopsided.

The two layouts are almost identical, and both have the same problems. The orange headline band and a letterboxed photo float in plain white, leaving large empty areas above, between and below them. The photo no longer runs edge to edge behind the band, so the original's layered, full-bleed look is gone and the result reads as two disconnected strips. The headline is also small for a tall vertical format. A's block sits noticeably above centre (about 150–567px), while B's (about 170–586px) is closer to centred, so B is marginally better balanced.

Both use the same layout. The photo is stacked over a text block indented to x≈165, which lines up with neither the photo's left edge nor the canvas centre. Stray decorative dots float around arbitrarily, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty dead space. A sits higher, leaving a larger empty band at the bottom. B moves the whole group down a little, so its vertical balance is marginally better, but the alignment and the large bottom gap are flawed in both.

Both have the same problems. The left arrow on the 'YOUR EFFICIENT' line is stretched into a big blurry smear. The light-blue side strip stops at a random height partway down. The 'YOUR EFFICIENT' line also sits far above 'ENERGY USE', leaving a large empty gap between them, with more dead space at the bottom. B is slightly better: its illustration keeps proper side margins and sits closer to the 'YOUR EFFICIENT' line, while A's illustration nearly touches the right edge of the canvas.

Both resizes are almost the same and broken in the same ways. The search-bar motif is split apart: an empty white pill floats on its own, the black search button has grown into a heavy blob at the top, and the headline sits outside the bar. The laptop and desk imagery is gone, leaving only cropped glasses and loose black arcs. The 'ОНЛАЙН-КУРС' subline is almost as large as the headline, so the two compete. The two differ only by a few pixels of vertical shift (B sits slightly higher, with marginally more room above the CTA), which isn't enough to separate them.

The two candidates are almost the same layout. Each puts the pen row up top and the 'STATIONERY SALE' headline below it, with a big empty red gap between them and a lot of dead space at the top and bottom. Each also leaves the original's trailing pencil orphaned in the bottom-left corner, cut off from everything else. A sits a few pixels lower and is slightly better centred; B sits slightly higher. Neither difference matters, so they rank the same.
